title: when the brief cites an owner decision key, have ork run adj check on it and say in the brief when it is not found

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
The reviewer reported this as tool feedback (deterministic-check) on ork in ork run ork-20261125-153910-3562, project ork, item S557:

when the brief cites an owner decision key, have ork run adj check on it and say in the brief when it is not found

Evidence: feedback.direction-duplicates is cited as an owner decision but adj check returns not found, per the implementer report

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body: Owner decisions (2026-11-25): Which brief text counts as citing an owner decision key, and what does ork say when `adj check` finds nothing? -> owner-decisions: only the `[key]` and `[key, adj N]` markers in the "Owner decisions" paragraph that `RecordSpecAnswers` writes (`internal/engine/speccheck.go:840-846`, carried into briefs at `internal/engine/round.go:662`). For each key without an adj id, ork runs `adj check KEY` and appends a line such as "adj check KEY: not found" to that brief section. Keys already carrying `adj N` are not re-checked. [brief.decision-key-check]. How should this slice's empty Files, Failing tests, Implement and Check sections say when it is done? -> tighten: fill the sections after the design answer. The Files section would name `internal/engine/brief.go`, `internal/engine/round.go` and their tests. One failing test would assert that a brief with an Owner decision citing a not-found key contains the "not found" line. A second would assert that a found key adds no line. The Check would be `go test ./internal/engine`, with all tests passing..
